noise.note: this capture set holds no second same-screen pair, so no differential noise baseline was available; the filter used is structural, and the Madden pair (known ground truth) is the control that proves it. A future capture should include one no-op pair per title.

madden09_ps2.question: does EE RAM hold the PLAY record in the bit-packed layout the disc uses

resident_database.note: the header, table directory and every table header and field directory are byte-identical to the disc; the divergence begins 22,436 bytes into PLAY's record array, i.e. after about 170 records

runtime_play_table.note: the record array does not follow its field directory the way a file does; 7,412 bytes separate them

schema_equality.compared: disc TEMPLATE.DAT member 2 PLAY vs both RAM field directories

ncaa09_ps2.question: where does the pre-game Home/Away uniform choice live, and is any of it on the disc
ncaa09_ps2.verdict: a 32-bit index in a two-element per-side game-setup record in the boot ELF's .data; its default is on the disc in the ELF, and it is in no database on the disc

record_array.found_by: the record head appears exactly twice in the ELF's .data initialiser, 76 bytes apart

second_data_flag.shape: one byte in a zero-initialised 0/1 array
second_data_flag.status: meaning not established; the array's members are scattered rather than paired per side, which is why it is not read as the choice

matchup_block.checked_against: two different matchups in this capture set; the ids read 67/35 in the state loading one fixture and 61/60 in the uniform-selector pair, matching the NCAA-06 school catalogue ids for those four schools

renderer_consequence.shape: a pair of heap pointers that exchange places

disc_correspondence.conclusion: the choice is written to no database row. What is on the disc is the default, as two initialised words in the boot ELF's .data at file offsets 0x00638F60 and 0x00638FAC.

ncaa09_ps2.assumption_that_would_make_this_wrong: that the choice is not also persisted to a memory-card save. This capture set holds no memory-card image, so persistence was not tested; a save written before and after the change would settle it.

unlocks.madden09: a two-state RAM diff on any EA TDB title now maps straight onto disc field offsets, so a field question is answered by pressing a button twice rather than by guessing at a schema
unlocks.ea_tdb_fleet: the same holds for the eight other EA TDB discs on the fleet: Madden NFL 2001, 2004, 06, 08, 09, 12 and NCAA Football 2004, 06, 09 all carry the same self-describing table format that RAM keeps verbatim
unlocks.ncaa09: the Uniforms page can state, with evidence, that the Home/Away selection is not a data row and owes no database lane; the editable surface stays the kit art

recommendations.section: 4a. Kits - the table that is not there
recommendations.change: add the RAM measurement: TEMPLATE.DAT member 0 is resident at EE 0x01D52AE0 with a 61,292-byte exact prefix, all four kit-shaped tables present with 0 rows, and 0 bytes differing across the whole resident extent when the on-screen uniform flips. The 'no equivalent' is now measured in the running game, not only on the disc.

note that the pre-game Home/Away selection is a 32-bit index at ELF .data +0x18 of a 76-byte per-side record (EE 0x00737F60 / 0x00737FAC, disc defaults 0 and 1 at ELF file offsets 0x00638F60 / 0x00638FAC), not a record in any table. It is an executable-data patch if anyone ever wants it, and it does not change the rung of either uniforms row.
